title: Good design hasn’t changed with AI — John Pham, SF Compute
talk_summary: A frontend/UX design talk about applying speed, trust, accessibility, and delight principles to web onboarding and purchase flows at a GPU cloud provider. It is almost entirely about human-facing UI craft, not agent orchestration, model routing, or review pipelines.

takeaways.technique: Perceived-latency budget as an explicit team objective
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat first paint under 300ms and 60fps as hard targets and put the current score on a visible scoreboard so the team optimizes it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The first paint happens in under 300 milliseconds. Most humans can only perceive stuff in under 400 milliseconds.

takeaways.what_they_do: They tell users upfront how many steps and how long a flow takes, and update progress as they go.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this will take three steps and this will take under a minute

takeaways.technique: Progressive disclosure to reduce cognitive load
takeaways.what_they_do: They split a form into three steps instead of one giant step to reduce cognitive load.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We want to reduce the cognitive load as a user goes through the onboarding.
